name: scan-broken-access-control
description: Scans applications, APIs, services, policies, and tests for broken access control risks such as missing authorization checks, IDOR/BOLA, privilege escalation, tenant isolation failures, unsafe CORS, path traversal, and overbroad object access.
instructions:
# scan-broken-access-control

Scans for authorization and privilege-boundary failures across applications and APIs.

## Orchestration

1. Load `references/rules.yaml` to get the active `BAC-` rule set.
2. Load `../_shared/owasp-cheatsheets.yaml` and use the mapped OWASP cheat sheets to support remediation guidance and references.
3. Identify target evidence from source code, configuration, tests, API specs, IaC, CI/CD, runtime manifests, and documentation relevant to the request.
4. Evaluate each rule using its `match_strategy`, preserving file path, line, snippet, control context, and confidence.
5. Mark each rule `Pass`, `Fail`, `Partial`, `Unknown`, or `Not Applicable` based on available evidence.
6. Prioritize findings by severity, exploitability, exposed surface, and whether a concrete remediation is available.
7. Render the final report using `references/report-template.md`.

## Usage

Scan the current repository:

```text
/scan-broken-access-control
```

Scan a specific path:

```text
/scan-broken-access-control src/ services/ docs/
```

## OWASP Cheat Sheets

Use the shared mapping in `../_shared/owasp-cheatsheets.yaml` for authoritative OWASP Cheat Sheet Series references that match this skill. Include the relevant cheat sheet links in the report when they directly support a finding or remediation.

## Review Guidance

Prioritize object-level authorization, tenant isolation, admin-only operations, and state-changing routes that depend only on client-controlled identifiers.

rules.name: Detect missing object-level authorization checks
rules.description: Identify handlers that load records by user-controlled ID without verifying ownership, tenant, or explicit permission.
rules.remediation: Add server-side object authorization checks for every object access path.

rules.name: Detect missing function-level authorization
rules.description: Identify privileged functions exposed without role, policy, or permission checks.
rules.remediation: Enforce deny-by-default authorization on privileged functions and administrative routes.

rules.name: Detect tenant boundary bypass
rules.description: Identify queries or routes missing tenant scoping in multi-tenant applications.
rules.remediation: Scope every data access by tenant or organization and test cross-tenant denial.

rules.name: Detect user-controlled role or permission changes
rules.description: Identify mass assignment or request fields that alter roles, ownership, or permissions.
rules.remediation: Allowlist mutable fields and protect role/permission transitions with policy checks.

rules.name: Detect unsafe path authorization
rules.description: Identify file access using untrusted path fragments without normalization and allowlisting.
rules.remediation: Normalize paths, enforce base directory constraints, and authorize file access.

rules.name: Detect permissive CORS with credentials
rules.description: Identify wildcard or reflected origins combined with credentialed requests.
rules.remediation: Use explicit origin allowlists and avoid credentials for broad origins.

rules.name: Detect predictable direct object references
rules.description: Identify exposed sequential IDs or direct references without authorization tests.
rules.remediation: Use authorization checks and add IDOR regression tests; opaque IDs help but do not replace auth.

rules.name: Detect missing default-deny policy
rules.description: Identify routers or middleware without a default authorization posture.
rules.remediation: Require authentication and authorization by default, then explicitly allow public routes.

rules.name: Detect BOLA in API routes
rules.description: Identify API endpoints where path/body IDs select resources without policy enforcement.
rules.remediation: Bind API access to subject, tenant, and resource permission checks.

rules.name: Detect method-level authorization gaps
rules.description: Identify routes where GET is protected but POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE variants are not.
rules.remediation: Apply authorization consistently across all HTTP methods and route aliases.

rules.name: Detect missing authorization tests
rules.description: Identify sensitive routes without negative tests for unauthorized, cross-user, or cross-tenant access.
rules.remediation: Add tests proving denial for unauthenticated, unauthorized, and cross-tenant requests.

rules.name: Detect public file or object storage exposure
rules.description: Identify public buckets, signed URL misuse, or unauthenticated file routes.
rules.remediation: Use private storage, short-lived scoped URLs, and server-side access checks.
